# The RT64 shaders the web page builds: one shader description a line, other mode L and H, color combiner L and H,
# flags, in hex. RT64 specializes each one's WGSL when the page is built and builds them with the game waiting: those
# above the first "section" line before the game starts, and a level's section when the level first draws with its
# shaders, so that nothing draws with the ubershader, which integrated graphics can't afford (N64Recomp-browser's
# docs/porting.md, Prebuilt shader lists).
#
# Recorded by code, not by playing: node lib/N64Recomp-browser/tools/record_shaders.mjs tools/shader_plan.json build/web
# roms/ddgq.us.z64 src/rt64_shaders.txt (its header says how), on tools/build_web.sh's page. Section 0 is the
# launcher, the boot (the logos and the title), the main menu, a new game's newscast and the world map (mapmonde),
# reached with Start and A as a player does. Then a section a level of the game's table of levels, each reached from
# the world map by tools/survey.js's go(), as the game's own exits change level, and walked about for 15 s of the
# game's time. The plan's last section, pause, goes into section 0: the pause menu, which comes up in any level and
# asks for its shaders a few at once, fewer than a section's build waits for, paused in trail. Not recorded: the
# levels past their starts, the bosses' fights and the game's other cutscenes. Flags follow settings (filtering, HDR,
# MSAA, upscaling), so a change to one of those defaults means recording again. Section 0's last line is added by
# hand, so keep it when recording again: the boot asks for it in some runs of the plan and not others (the recording
# didn't, three of a page's boot checks, the plan's first 20 s, did).
